detectors.description: Singapore NRIC and FIN numbers: prefix S, T, F, G or M, seven digits, and a check letter that must pass the checksum. Case-insensitive.

NRIC/FIN shape with a check letter that fails the checksum: a mistyped NRIC or an NRIC-shaped look-alike such as an order number. Lower confidence than NRIC; each consumer decides how to treat it (ADR 0006).

Singapore phone numbers: eight digits starting 3 (internet telephony), 6 (fixed line), 8 or 9 (mobile) per the IMDA National Numbering Plan, optionally split 4-4 by a space or hyphen, optionally preceded by +65, (65), (+65), 0065 or 65.
Email addresses: a local part of letters, digits and . _ % + -, an @, and a domain whose last label is two or more letters. Deliberately permissive: domains may start with a digit.

Payment card numbers: 13 to 19 digits, optionally grouped by single spaces or hyphens, that pass the Luhn checksum and start with a prefix used by Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover, JCB, UnionPay or Diners Club, at a length that network issues.

Singapore postal codes: six digits with a valid postal sector (01 to 82, except 74), only after an address clue: "Singapore" (any case), "S" or "S(" directly before the digits, or a key such as postal code, postalCode, postcode or zip followed by an optional colon or equals sign and quotes. Only the six digits are reported; the clue is context (ADR 0010, ADR 0011).
